reconstruction.product_guess: Neon Warden, a browser-based top-down vertical bullet-hell shoot-'em-up vertical slice where resting your weapon charges a shot and scans enemies, allowing pacifist or disarming playstyles.
reconstruction.how_to_get_it: Play it directly in a web browser with no installation at adamsmith.systems.
reconstruction.question_raised: What happens if you reach The Warden without ever firing a single shot ('weapon status: cold'), and what is the true agenda of the Lane Authority?
uncertain: What 'CM121 f26' on the final card refers to (likely a university course code and term, e.g., Fall 2026).
How 'breaking the gun' is mechanically executed versus destroying the whole ship (whether it requires aiming at specific hitboxes or using the charged shot after scanning).

scores.evidence: Starts immediately in bullet-hell gameplay at 00:00-00:05, reveals the title 'NEON WARDEN' at 00:06, and well over 60% of the runtime is direct player-view gameplay.

Text cards ('TAP. HOLD. REST TO CHARGE.' at 00:07, 'RESTING SCANS THEM.' at 00:17, 'BREAK THE GUN. SPARE THE SHIP.' at 00:26, 'OR NEVER FIRE AT ALL.' at 01:17) are hyper-specific to this game's mechanics and cleanly intercut on dark backgrounds.

Charging and firing is clear at 00:09-00:12, scanning shows the 'Codex: Scout' pop-up at 00:19-00:20, and grazing shows the score multiplier ticking up at 00:23-00:25. However, 'BREAK THE GUN. SPARE THE SHIP.' (00:26-00:36) is visually hard to read in-shot because the tiny left-side radio pop-up at 00:34 is too small and fast to notice while watching the ship.

Several sectors and setups repeat across the first 37 seconds: Sector 4 appears at 00:00, 00:04, and 00:23; Sector 1 appears at 00:09 and 00:32; Sector 2 appears at 00:13 and 00:19; Sector 5 appears at 00:02 and 00:35.

The narrative sequence from 00:37 to 01:04 holds for 27 seconds with minimal gameplay action (an angled camera flight from 00:37-00:44, a slow boss descent from 00:45-00:54, and a static dialogue standoff from 00:55-01:04).
The pacifist route ('OR NEVER FIRE AT ALL.' at 01:17) is brilliantly teased at 01:19-01:24 with The Warden asking 'Why is your gun cold?!' without spoiling the resolution.

Bullet-hell dodges at 00:02 and 00:23 work well as 1-second clips, but many shots have dark, sparse backgrounds and small geometric sprites (e.g., 00:13, 00:28, 00:38) that lack visual punch as standalone 1-second microtrailer fragments.
At 01:27-01:30, the end card clearly states 'A vertical slice. Play it in your browser. No install. adamsmith.systems'.

The first 36 seconds move briskly, but pacing stalls during the 27-second cutscene/dialogue block (00:37-01:04), especially the 7-second static angled shot at 00:37-00:44 and the 10-second boss descent at 00:45-00:54.

fixes.problem: The 27-second narrative build-up (00:37-01:04) drags the pacing down because 00:37-00:44 is a static angled shot of the ship where nothing happens visually, followed by a slow 10-second boss entrance.
fixes.fix: Cut 00:37-00:44 entirely (saving the 'weapon status: cold' reveal solely for the 01:17 twist) and overlap the 'Lane Authority Briefing' voiceover (00:45-00:52) onto the final gameplay montage shots (00:32-00:36) so the boss appears and speaks immediately at the drop.

fixes.problem: After the 'BREAK THE GUN. SPARE THE SHIP.' card at 00:26, the visual receipt of sparing an enemy is hard to see because the enemy sprites are small and the 'Unit 2290A [sparing]' radio text at 00:34 is tiny on the far left edge.
fixes.fix: Punch in (zoom in) on the capture at 00:28-00:34 or add a clear on-screen callout showing the turret breaking off while the ship flies away unharmed and transmits its message.

fixes.problem: The opening 5 seconds repeat Sector 4 twice (00:00-00:01 and 00:04-00:05) with sparse enemy waves, which is less visually gripping than the dense bullet patterns shown later.
fixes.fix: Start the trailer with the dense pink bullet-curtain shot at 00:02 and the boss bullet pattern from 01:05 to immediately hook viewers, removing the duplicate Sector 4 shot at 00:04.

overall.summary: A smart, well-structured vertical slice trailer with a great Undertale-style pacifist twist and crystal-clear mechanic cards, held back mainly by a slow 27-second mid-trailer dialogue build-up and some repetitive/visually sparse early shots.
